title: Pre-Analysis — Aft Pylon Fairing Heat Shield and Interface Seal Renewal
abstract: Original pre-analysis for the ventilated heat shield and thicker interface seal at the aft pylon fairing on Auran-powered twin-engine aircraft, closed clean with a repair interaction and one maintenance action.

sections.objective: Establish whether the ventilated heat shield and the thicker interface seal can be installed on the existing fairing structure without disturbing approved repairs or other work in the pylon bay, following the scorching reports that showed hot gas recirculating into the fairing cavity. The work order had to check the composite repair population on the fairing skin and confirm that nothing else routinely installed in the same access area constrains the new shield envelope.
sections.findings_summary: Two items are real and one of them is a genuine geometric constraint. The composite scarf repair for heat and impact damage is written for the current skin lay-up and its scarf ratio assumes the present cavity temperature; a fairing carrying a scarf repair under the new shield sees a different soak profile than the repair was substantiated for, and the repair population on Auran-powered aircraft is not small. The installation task carries the seal compression figures and the shield fastener sequence and both change outright, which makes it the first document to revise. The third result came from the zone link rather than from any wording: the green system engine driven pump is removed and installed through the same pylon access, and its removal task calls for the fairing to be open, so the two pieces of work compete for the same slot during a check.
sections.next_steps: Ask the composite repair owner to state whether a scarf repair remains valid under the ventilated shield, and to give a temperature limit rather than a case-by-case answer. Revise the fairing installation task with the new seal compression and fastener sequence as the first manual action. Note the shared access with the hydraulic pump work in the retrofit bulletin so that operators can plan one fairing opening instead of two.

similarity_seeds: thermal distortion of an interface seal allowing hot gas recirculation
scorching found in a pylon fairing cavity at a routine check

tasks.title: Establish the composite repair population on the fairing skin
Review the fairing installation acceptance figures
Check other work using the same pylon access

evidence.similarity_note: Same fairing part set by entity link, and the similarity search returns it on heat damage wording shared with the reason for change.

expected_findings.rationale: The scarf repair is substantiated against the present cavity soak temperature. A ventilated shield changes that profile, and a fairing carrying a scarf repair would be operating outside the conditions the repair was approved for.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a temperature limit from the composite repair owner rather than a case-by-case answer.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task carries the seal compression figures and the shield fastener sequence. Both change outright with the thicker seal, and the task is the working document for every fairing refit on the line.
expected_findings.resolution: Revise as the first manual action once the design is frozen.

expected_findings.rationale: The engine driven pump is installed through the same pylon access and its task requires the fairing to be open. Nothing in the two documents shares vocabulary, but they compete for the same aircraft slot and the same access panel during a check.
expected_findings.resolution: Note the shared access in the retrofit bulletin so operators plan one fairing opening.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the whole fairing part set and both zones and is returned immediately alongside the installation task. Removal is unaffected: the shield comes away with the fairing and no removal step references the seal compression or the fastener sequence that the change touches.

type_data.conclusion: The renewal is sound. One repair interaction needs a temperature limit and the installation task must be revised; no design change is required.
